entries.title: Introduction to Our Body
entries.teacher_activities: i. Teacher uses songs and rhymes to introduce body parts. ii.Teacher points to and names body parts (head, hands, legs, face, body). iii.Teacher uses charts and pictures to show the body. iv.Teacher guides pupils to touch and identify their own body parts. v. Teacher shows pictures of clean, healthy children.
entries.pupil_activities: i.Pupils sing body parts songs. ii. Pupils point to their body parts. iii.Pupils touch their body parts when named. iv.Pupils look at pictures of children. v. Pupils say "body" with teacher.
entries.learning_resources: Charts Pictures Dolls Mirrors Body parts poster Video clips

entries.title: Care of the Skin I - Bathing Regularly
entries.teacher_activities: i. Teacher uses charts and video clips to explain bathing in simple terms. ii. Teacher demonstrates bathing using a doll with water, soap, and sponge. iii.Teacher sings bathing songs ("This is the way we wash our body"). iv. Teacher emphasizes bathing every day. v. Teacher shows pictures of children taking baths.
entries.pupil_activities: i.Pupils watch bathing demonstration. ii.Pupils sing bathing songs. iii.Pupils mime washing their body. iv.Pupils identify water, soap, and sponge. v. Pupils practice with dolls.
entries.learning_resources: Doll Basin Water Soap Sponge Towel Charts Pictures Video clips

_source.raw_topic: Care of the Skin I - Bathing Regularly

entries.title: Care of the Skin II - Applying Body Cream
entries.teacher_activities: i. Teacher demonstrates drying body with towel after bathing using a doll. ii.Teacher shows how to apply body cream and hair cream. iii.Teacher lets pupils touch and smell body cream. iv. Teacher emphasizes applying cream after bathing. v. Teacher shows pictures of children applying cream.
entries.pupil_activities: i. Pupils mime drying their body. ii.Pupils pretend to apply body cream. iii.Pupils touch body cream containers. iv.Pupils identify towel and cream. v. Pupils practice on dolls.
entries.learning_resources: Towel Body cream Hair cream Lotion Charts Pictures Dolls Video clips

_source.raw_topic: Care of the Skin II - Applying Body Cream

entries.title: Care of the Skin III - Materials Used
entries.teacher_activities: i. Teacher identifies and displays materials used for skin care (soap, sponge, towel, body cream, hair cream). ii.Teacher names each material clearly and repeatedly. iii. Teacher demonstrates use of each material. iv. Teacher guides pupils to identify materials. v. Teacher plays identification games with materials.
entries.pupil_activities: i. Pupils identify materials used to take care of the skin. ii.Pupils point to each material when named. iii.Pupils touch and hold materials safely. iv.Pupils match materials to their uses. v. Pupils participate in "Find the..." games.
entries.learning_resources: Soap Sponge Towel Body cream Hair cream Charts Pictures Sorting baskets

entries.title: Clean and Dirty Environments - Causes of Dirty Environment
entries.teacher_activities: i. Teacher shows pictures of actions that make environment dirty (throwing trash on floor, spilling things, not putting toys away). ii.Teacher demonstrates "wrong" actions and says "No, no." iii. Teacher shows video clips of littering and messiness. iv.Teacher explains these cause dirty environment in simple terms. v. Teacher emphasizes not doing these things.
entries.pupil_activities: i. Pupils identify actions that make places dirty. ii.Pupils shake heads "no" for bad actions. iii.Pupils understand throwing trash is wrong. iv. Pupils recognize causes of mess. v. Pupils say "no" to dirty actions.

entries.title: Clean and Dirty Environments - Effects and Importance
entries.teacher_activities: i. Teacher shows effects of dirty environment (flies, bad smell, sickness, ugly places) using pictures. ii.Teacher shows importance of clean environment (healthy, beautiful, happy, safe) using pictures. iii.Teacher uses happy children in clean places vs sad faces in dirty places. iv.Teacher emphasizes clean is good, dirty is bad in very simple terms. v. Teacher praises clean habits.
entries.pupil_activities: i. Pupils identify happy children in clean places. ii.Pupils understand clean environment is good. iii. Pupils make happy faces for clean places. iv.Pupils understand dirty can make us sick. v. Pupils prefer clean environments.

entries.title: Personal Hygiene - Meaning and Importance
entries.teacher_activities: i.Teacher explains "personal hygiene" as "keeping our body clean" in very simple terms. ii. Teacher shows pictures of clean, well- groomed children. iii.Teacher reviews all hygiene practices learned (bathing, brushing teeth, clean clothes). iv.Teacher emphasizes importance (healthy, look good, feel good, no germs). v. Teacher uses songs about being clean.
entries.pupil_activities: i. Pupils understand personal hygiene means clean body. ii.Pupils identify clean, neat children in pictures. iii.Pupils list hygiene practices with guidance. iv.Pupils understand being clean is important. v. Pupils sing cleanliness songs.
entries.learning_resources: Pictures of groomed children Charts Video clips Posters Dolls

entries.title: Personal Hygiene - How to Maintain Good Personal Hygiene

Teacher reviews all hygiene materials.

entries.title: Good Health - Meaning
entries.teacher_activities: i.Teacher explains "good health" as "feeling strong and well" in simple terms. ii.Teacher shows pictures of healthy, active children vs sick children. iii.Teacher asks pupils to show strong arms/muscles. iv.Teacher uses happy, energetic actions to show good health. v. Teacher emphasizes being healthy is wonderful.
entries.pupil_activities: i.Pupils understand good health means feeling well. ii.Pupils identify healthy children in pictures. iii. Pupils show their strong arms/muscles. iv.Pupils jump, run (safely) to show they are healthy. v. Pupils make happy faces for good health.
entries.learning_resources: Pictures of healthy children Charts Video clips Posters

entries.title: Good Health - Good Food
entries.teacher_activities: i. Teacher shows pictures of good, nutritious food (fruits, vegetables, rice, beans, fish, eggs, milk). ii.Teacher explains good food makes us strong and healthy. iii.Teacher shows clean food vs dirty food. iv.Teacher lets pupils identify healthy foods. v. Teacher emphasizes eating good food every day.
entries.pupil_activities: i. Pupils identify good, healthy foods. ii. Pupils point to fruits and vegetables. iii. Pupils understand good food helps us grow. iv.Pupils mime eating good food. v. Pupils choose healthy food pictures.
entries.learning_resources: Pictures of healthy foods Toy foods Real fruits (for display) Charts Posters

entries.title: Good Health - Body Exercise and Rest
entries.teacher_activities: i.Teacher demonstrates simple exercises (stretching, jumping, running in place, dancing). ii.Teacher shows pictures of children playing and exercising. iii.Teacher explains exercise makes us strong. iv.Teacher demonstrates resting and sleeping. v.Teacher explains we need sleep to be healthy and strong. vi. Teacher shows pictures of children sleeping peacefully.
entries.pupil_activities: i.Pupils participate in simple exercises. ii. Pupils stretch, jump, and move safely. iii.Pupils understand exercise is good for body. iv.Pupils mime sleeping and resting. v.Pupils understand we need rest/sleep. vi. Pupils enjoy movement activities.

entries.teacher_activities: Number Concepts: i. The teacher introduces the concept of counting using real objects (fingers, pencils, books). ii.The teacher counts from 0-5 aloud slowly with pupils. iii.The teacher shows number cards 0-5 and names each number. iv.The teacher demonstrates one- to-one correspondence by touching objects while counting. Counting Activities: i. The teacher uses counting songs like "One, Two, Buckle My Shoe" ii.The teacher counts familiar classroom objects (chairs, tables, pupils). iii. The teacher plays counting games with pupils. Songs/Rhymes: i.The teacher teaches "Five Little Ducks" ii.The teacher uses finger counting rhymes. iii. The teacher demonstrates counting with actions.
